title: Boundary Quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov Equations and Integrability of Quantum Field Theories with Time-Dependent Bulk and Boundary Coupling Strengths
abstract: The generalized Bethe ansatz framework formulated in [P. R. Pasnoori, Phys. Rev. B 112, L060409 (2025)] provides a unified framework to find exact solutions to quantum many-body systems with time-dependent coupling strengths with periodic boundary conditions. In this work we extend this framework to the case of open boundary conditions where in addition to the time-dependent interactions in the bulk, the boundary conditions are explicitly time-dependent. We show that for integrable time-dependent bulk coupling strengths, the generalized Bethe ansatz framework provides the time-dependent boundary conditions compatible with integrability and reduces the time-dependent Schrodinger equation to a set of matrix difference equations called the boundary quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov (BqKZ) equations. The solution to the BqKZ equations provides the explicit form of the exact wavefunction. We further show that the RG invariants of the corresponding static model identify with the dynamical invariants in the time-dependent model.
summary: This work develops an extension of the generalized Bethe ansatz to handle quantum field theories with time-dependent interactions at both the bulk and the boundaries. By enforcing integrability, the system's dynamics are constrained to satisfy boundary quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov (BqKZ) equations. This provides an exact, powerful method for determining the time-dependent wavefunction in complex, open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper extends the generalized Bethe ansatz framework to find exact solutions for quantum field theories with both time-dependent bulk and explicitly time-dependent boundary coupling strengths while maintaining integrability.
main_result: The consistency of the wavefunction requires the system to satisfy boundary quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov (BqKZ) equations, which govern the exact time-dependent wavefunction.
method: The authors employ the generalized Bethe ansatz, requiring the bulk and boundary S-matrices to satisfy the reflection equation to ensure integrability.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on the SU(2) Gross-Neveu model, described by a time-dependent Schrödinger equation for fermions confined between boundaries (open boundary conditions).
key_observables: The exact many-body wavefunction, the conserved total number of fermions (N), and the dynamical invariants ($\chi_L, \chi_R$).
important_parameters: Time-dependent coupling strengths $g(t)$ and boundary coupling functions $B(t)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the case of diagonal boundaries, which breaks $Z_2$ spin flip and $SU(2)$ spin rotation symmetry but preserves $U(1)$ symmetry.
paper_structure: The structure progresses from establishing the generalized Bethe ansatz for time-dependent bulk interactions to incorporating time-dependent boundary conditions. This leads to deriving the necessary reflection equations (for the boundaries) and subsequently constructing the matrix difference equations known as the BqKZ equations.
why_interesting: The connection between integrable quantum field theories, time-dependent boundary conditions, and the resulting matrix difference equations (BqKZ) provides powerful, exact tools for analyzing open quantum systems dynamics, which is highly relevant to modern AMO and open quantum system research.
